New!
  
We’re introducing a brand-new Multi-Rental Calendar — designed to help you manage 10–100 rentals with more clarity, speed, and control.

What’s new?
Smooth horizontal scrolling through dates
Vertical browsing with up to 50 rentals at once
Filters for rental, destination, tag, amenities & more
A brand-new booking pill design with hover tooltips

— The Smily Team 💙

articles.author: Eduardo, Head of Product
articles.description:
New!
  
We’ve just launched a brand-new Rate Simulator designed to give you complete visibility into nightly pricing—and the power to simulate booking quotes in just a few clicks.

Whether you’re reviewing your pricing, planning special offers, or answering guest questions, you’ll now have the clarity you need—without switching tabs or tools.
What’s new?
A clean, monthly calendar view showing nightly base rates per rental
Minimum stay rules displayed directly under each date (e.g. “7 ☾”)
“No rates” clearly flagged with tooltips when pricing is missing
An integrated Rate Simulator to test quotes based on:
Stay dates
Guest count
Booking source (e.g. Direct, Airbnb)

Simulate and see it all
Use the simulator to get an instant breakdown of what makes up the initial price—including rate rules, channel markups, special offers, and rounding. You’ll immediately see how the price is built—and why.
If something can’t be calculated, we’ll show you exactly what’s missing so you can fix it fast.
This is just the beginning…
We’re listening to your feedback and fine-tuning things continuously—bug fixes, improvements, and new features are on the way.
— The Smily Team 💙
articles.title: The New Rate Simulator Is Here — Clearer Prices, Faster Answers

articles.author: Eduardo, Head of Product
articles.description:
New!
  
We’re excited to launch Google Analytics (GA4) Tracking for your Smily-powered website.
This new feature gives you end-to-end visibility on your direct bookings, helping you track conversions, optimize your marketing ROI, and reduce OTA dependency.
What’s New?
Full Conversion Tracking — Track every booking type: instant, inquiry-based, or manual.
Multi-Session Tracking — See the complete guest journey, even across multiple sessions.
Rich Purchase Events — Automatically send booking ID, rental details, payment info, and more to your GA4.
Smooth Redirection After Payment — Guests are sent back to your domain post-payment—ensuring seamless tracking and a smooth experience.
Important:
This feature is only available if you’re using a Smily-powered website.
If you don’t have one yet and want to boost your direct bookings with these insights, contact your Account Manager to get started.
Why It Matters?
Optimize your marketing spend by tracking which campaigns convert.
Spot and fix booking funnel drop-offs to streamline booking journey & improve conversions.
Make smarter decisions to grow your direct bookings and reduce reliance on OTAs.
Get Started Today
Ensure you have a Google Analytics 4 account & setup.
Add your Google Analytics 4 tag in your Smily website (via the Preferences tab)
You will then be setup to start making data-driven decisions to supercharge your direct bookings. For any questions, feel free to contact your account manager.
— The Smily Team 💙
articles.title: Introducing GA Tracking: Unlock the Power of Your Booking Data for Smily-powered website

Description: Tailnets using shared public email providers
What happened?
On May 22, 2025 our Reddit community gave us the necessary kick
to address an issue with handling shared public email provider domains ("shared
domains"). We mitigated the risk for new tailnets being created on previously
unknown shared domains by enabling user approval by
default. This issue affects only a small portion of our user base, and this
bulletin provides some background, mitigation steps, and our future plans.
Background
Tailscale users are mapped to tailnets by their email address domain (with a
few exceptions*). This means that user1@example.com and user2@example.com
can both log in to tailnet example.com. We chose this default behavior because
it reduces onboarding friction for new users and tailnet admi…
articles.title: TS-2025-004

articles.description:
Description: Insecure non-constant time comparison in DERP server mesh authentication
What happened?
Tailscale's DERP (Designated Encrypted Relay for Packets) servers provide connectivity between Tailscale nodes in the event that they cannot mutually communicate due to network restrictions. DERP servers deployed in the same region communicate using a private mesh API to coordinate client connections amongst themselves. These private mesh connections authenticate using a pre-shared secret key.
The DERP servers previously used an insecure non-constant time comparison when verifying the mesh authentication secret. This would have allowed an attacker to discover the mesh secret by performing a side channel timing attack.
The issue was present since the introduction of DERP meshing and patched on May 21, 2025. We have updated all Tailscale-managed DERP servers and rotated their mesh secrets.
Who was affected?
All Tailscale-operated DERP servers and Tailscale users who operate their own custom DERP servers with more than one server per region.
What was the impact?
An attacker who discovered the mesh key could not see any plaintext traffic between nodes, since all traffic is end-to-end encrypted.
An attacker with mesh access would have been able to enumerate all peers connected to a DERP server, including their WireGuard public key and their source IP address and port.
An attacker with mesh access would have been able to perform a denial-of-service attack (DoS attack), prohibiting a node’s keys on any DERP servers by forcing disconnects of meshed DERP servers by using the ClosePeer API.
We have no evidence to indicate any abuse of this issue.
What do I need to do?
If you operate your own custom DERP servers in a mesh setup, you should update to the latest version and rotate any mesh keys that were previously in use.
articles.title: TS-2025-003

articles.description:
Description: Privilege escalation in proxy-to-grafana via header spoofing
What happened?
The Tailscale Grafana proxy is a HTTP reverse proxy for Grafana that annotates requests with X-Webauth-* headers bearing the requesting user's whois-based Tailscale identity.
The Grafana proxy is intended to be used in combination with Grafana's session-based authentication using cookies issued in response to requests made to /login to authenticate subsequent requests to other endpoints.
When configured to use session-based authentication, Grafana's /api/ routes will continue to accept X-Webauth-* headers for authentication. Previous versions of the Grafana proxy did not strip these X-Webauth-* headers from API requests allowing them to be forged by a malicious tailnet node.
The issue was present since the initial release of the Grafana proxy, and was patched on May 15th, 2025. The Grafana proxy now strips X-Webauth-* headers from all incoming requests.
Who was affected?
Tailnets using Grafana in combination with the Grafana proxy to authenticate users.
What was the impact?
Grafana instances protected by the Grafana proxy would have been vulnerable to privilege escalation via HTTP request header forgery from members of their tailnet.
What do I need to do?
Update to the latest Grafana proxy by running go install tailscale.com/cmd/proxy-to-grafana@latest
Credits
Thanks to Yeongrok Gim for reporting this issue.
articles.title: TS-2025-002

Incident began at 2025-05-22 17:00 and ended at 2025-05-23 01:45 (times are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC)).

Mini Incident Report

We apologize for the inconvenience this service disruption/outage may have caused. We would like to provide some information about this incident below. Please note, this information is based on our best knowledge at the time of posting and is subject to change as our investigation continues. If you have experienced impact outside of what is listed below, please reach out to Google Cloud Support using https://cloud.google.com/support or to Google Workspace Support using help article https://support.google.com/a/answer/1047213.

(All Times US/Pacific)

Incident Start: 22 May, 2025 10:00

Incident End: 22 May, 2025 18:45

Duration: 8 hours, 45 minutes

Affected Services and Features:

AppSheet

Regions/Zones: Global

Description: AppSheet in Looker Studio experienced issues where applications and dashboards were not visible. Based on our analysis, this was caused by a recent change that AppSheet introduced to enhance its authentication for the Looker Studio connector. Once the impact was identified by our Engineering team, we promptly rolled back the change, restoring the connector's stability.

Customer Impact: Impacted customers may have experienced AppSheet apps not showing within Looker Studio, and dependent dashboards may have returned an exception: ‘Community Connector Error’.

Affected products: AppSheet

Resolved - On May 28, 2025, from approximately 09:45 UTC to 14:45 UTC, GitHub Actions experienced delayed job starts for workflows in public repos using Ubuntu-24 standard hosted runners. This was caused by a misconfiguration in backend caching behavior after a failover, which led to duplicate job assignments and reduced available capacity. Approximately 19.7% of Ubuntu-24 hosted runner jobs on public repos were delayed.  Other hosted runners, self-hosted runners, and private repo workflows were unaffected.
By 12:45 UTC, we mitigated the issue by redeploying backend components to reset state and scaling up available resources to more quickly work through the backlog of queued jobs. We are working to improve our deployment and failover resiliency and validation to reduce the likelihood of similar issues in the future.

articles.description: On June 1, 2025, beginning around 5:00 PM PDT until 6:29 PM PDT, some users experienced issues with connecting to or logging into Slack, sending or receiving messages including those that were scheduled, and trouble loading items such as 'Activity' view.We traced the issue to a backend caching system that began improperly serving traffic in one of our database regions. As a result, an increase in error rates occurred for many Slack features. An automated recovery system began shifting failed requests to healthy databases, allowing success for some users.To fully mitigate the impact, we temporarily rerouted traffic away from the affected backend service, allowing it to recover. After addressing the issue with the caching system, we directed traffic back to the service once it was functioning properly, resolving the issue for all affected users.
articles.title: Incident: Trouble connecting to Slack

articles.description: From Sunday June 1, 2025 at 11:30 PM PDT, to Monday June 2, 2025 at 1:09 PM PDT, some Org Owners/Admins were unable to see a complete list of their org workspaces from the admin dashboard. A recent code change relating to how workspaces are displayed on the admin dashboard was inadvertently hiding certain workspaces from view. We reverted this change, which fully resolved the issue.
articles.title: Incident: Some users may be experiencing issues with organizational dashboards not loading correctly.

articles.description: On May 12, 2025 between 15:00 PDT and 16:58 PDT users experienced issues with sending messages, loading channels and interacting with agents.This was due to elevated error rates across our platform caused by an issue with the communication link between our web application and the database routing layer. Due to recent infrastructure growth, we exceeded some defined configurations which prevented our web application from receiving updates about available database gateways/communication links.Our engineering team addressed the issue by making infrastructure adjustments; enabling web applications to receive the complete, updated list of database gateways and restoring normal operations.
articles.title: Outage: Users experiencing issues connecting to Slack and unable to load threads

articles.description: From May 5, 2025 at around 8:22 AM PDT until May 7, 2025 at 10:36 AM PDT, users may have experienced missing notifications in open channels and direct messages.We traced this issue to a recent code change that incorrectly set the window focus state. As a result, Slack mistakenly treated some windows as active which prevented notifications from triggering as expected. The underlying bug in the focus state logic was corrected, restoring normal notification behavior for all affected users.If you are still experiencing issues, please refresh your Slack app using Cmd + Shift + R (Mac) or Ctrl + Shift + R (Windows/Linux).
articles.title: Incident: Some users are not receiving notifications for channel messages or DMs when the channel or DM is open

articles.description: On May 2, 2025 from 4:34 PM PDT to May 5th, 2025 at 12:24 PM PDT, users may have had trouble switching to the Archived or the Completed views of the Later tab, as well as problems marking their items as archived or completed.We made a code change that inadvertently prevented state changes for Later items. We rolled back this change, restoring full functionality to this feature.
articles.title: Incident: Some users may be having trouble with the Later tab on the desktop app and browser.

articles.description: On May 5, 2025 from 2:41 PM PDT until 10:31 PM PDT, users experienced issues affecting message sending and Threads functionality. The issues stemmed from a code change that incorrectly routed database queries to primary servers instead of replicas, causing instability in our database infrastructure.The incident was automatically detected when our database management system encountered issues with its operations. Our engineering teams identified the root cause and implemented a fix by reverting the problematic code change. Service was fully restored after the code reversion.We apologise for any disruption this may have caused.
